issue: Gaussian signed wavelength offsets used pow(z,2.) in three production GLSL materials. Negative-base pow is undefined even for the float exponent 2.
repair: One shared LINE_SPECTRUM_GLSL computes z=(wavelength-centers)/widths and exp(-0.5*(z*z)). All three production materials include it.
model_preservation: Reference wavelength centers 610/545/455 nm, widths 35/30/25 nm, Doppler/beaming, ray geometry and adopted Schwarzschild/Minkowski/native-FTD boundaries are unchanged.
source_hash_convention: SHA-256 of UTF-8 source with CRLF normalized to LF, matching Git text normalization.

reproduction_before_repair.interpretation: The tested GPU passed the old expressions. That observation does not establish language-defined behavior or portability.

not_rerun: Full native C++/CUDA and theory Python campaigns

actual_gpu_gaussian.method: Clone each full production WebGL material, rename only its main entry point, and expose the unchanged production spectrum(wavelength) function to an RGBA32F target. Read actual framebuffer pixels; no CPU shader translation or screenshots are used as GPU evidence.

hardware.renderer: ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (0x00002B85) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)

actual_gpu_gaussian.sign_coverage: Negative, zero and positive normalized offsets for every response channel.
